name: Grace Whitfield
extracurriculars: Robotics captain; Science Olympiad; orchestra
essay_prompt: Describe a challenge you have faced and what you learned from it.
essay_text: Our robotics team lost its mentor in October, three weeks before regionals. I was vice-captain and suddenly nobody knew how to run the CNC mill. I spent two weekends reading the manual and ruined about forty dollars of aluminum before I got a clean cut. What I actually learned was not machining. It was that I had been waiting for someone to tell me the team was allowed to keep going. Nobody was going to. We placed fourth and I stopped waiting for permission after that.
recommendation_summary: Top student in a competitive class. Teachers describe her as the person who figures out what needs doing before being asked.
financial_need_statement: Two-parent household, one income after a layoff in 2024. Family contribution estimated at $4,000/yr.

name: Priya Raghunathan
extracurriculars: Math team; hospital volunteer; tutors ESL students
essay_prompt: Describe a challenge you have faced and what you learned from it.
essay_text: I tutored a seventh grader named Hector in math for two years. For the first six months I was terrible at it. I would explain a problem the way it made sense to me, he would nod, and then he would get the next one wrong. The breakthrough was when I stopped explaining and started asking him to explain to me. His reasoning was not wrong, it was built on a definition of a fraction he had learned incorrectly in fourth grade. I had been patching symptoms. I think about that a lot now when I debug my own code.
recommendation_summary: Exceptional analytical ability paired with unusual patience. Has quietly built the peer tutoring program into something the department depends on.
financial_need_statement: Household of five, single earner. Applying to in-state schools for cost reasons.

name: Marcus Okonkwo
extracurriculars: Varsity track; church youth leader; food bank
essay_prompt: Describe a challenge you have faced and what you learned from it.
essay_text: I work twenty hours a week at a pharmacy counter and most of what I do is tell people their medication costs more than they expected. There is a specific silence when someone is deciding which prescription to leave behind. The first few months I took it home with me. My manager told me something useful, which is that I could not fix the price but I could always check whether a generic existed, and most people did not know to ask. It is a small lever. I would like a bigger one, which is most of why I am applying.
recommendation_summary: Carries a heavy work schedule without letting it show in his academics. Natural leader; younger students gravitate to him.
financial_need_statement: Six-person household, contributes to family income. Significant need.

name: Sofia Ramirez
extracurriculars: Cross country; community garden project; debate
essay_prompt: Describe a challenge you have faced and what you learned from it.
essay_text: In sophomore year I started a composting program at school and it failed completely. I had signs, I had bins, I had a slideshow. Within two months the bins were full of chip bags and someone had put a shoe in one. I assumed people did not care about composting. I was wrong. Nobody knew what counted as compostable and I had never asked. The second attempt had pictures instead of words and a student from each lunch period standing by the bins for the first two weeks. It works now. The lesson was that I had designed it for people like me.
recommendation_summary: Persistent in a way that is rare at this age. Willing to be publicly wrong and try again.
financial_need_statement: First-generation college student. Family of four, both parents employed hourly.

extracurriculars: Auto shop; FIRST Robotics; part-time mechanic
essay_prompt: Describe a challenge you have faced and what you learned from it.
essay_text: My dad's shop closed when I was sixteen and I spent that summer helping him sell off the lifts and the diagnostic scanner. He had run it for nineteen years. What struck me was that the thing that killed it was not a lack of skill. He could fix anything. He could not read the new cars, the ones where the fault lives in software and the dealer holds the key. I have been teaching myself CAN bus protocols since then, partly out of spite. I would like to be the kind of engineer who does not lock people out of their own machines.
recommendation_summary: Genuinely gifted with mechanical systems. Self-taught well beyond the curriculum we offer.
financial_need_statement: Single-parent household following business closure. High need.

name: Ananya Deshpande
extracurriculars: Research intern at UAB; violin; Model UN
essay_prompt: Describe a challenge you have faced and what you learned from it.
essay_text: I spent last summer in a lab pipetting the same assay for nine weeks. The honest version is that I was bored for most of it and felt guilty about being bored. Around week seven a postdoc showed me the notebook from the failed version of the experiment, three years of it, and I understood that the tedium was the point, or at least the cost. Science is mostly a record of things that did not work, kept carefully enough that the next person does not repeat them. I am less impatient now. I am also a much better note-taker.
recommendation_summary: Intellectually serious and refreshingly honest about her own limitations. Strong candidate for research.
financial_need_statement: Both parents employed; sibling currently in college. Moderate need.

name: Imani Robinson
extracurriculars: Speech and debate; city youth council; yearbook editor

essay_text: I got appointed to the city youth council expecting to talk about a skate park. name: Minh Nguyen
extracurriculars: Math club; family restaurant; volunteer translator
essay_prompt: Describe a challenge you have faced and what you learned from it.
essay_text: I translate for my parents at doctor's appointments and have since I was about eleven. For a long time I thought the hard part was vocabulary. It is not. The hard part is that a doctor will say something with a hedge in it, something like this is probably nothing but we should check, and there is no clean way to carry the hedge across. Translate it too strong and my mother panics. Too soft and she skips the follow-up. I have gotten it wrong both directions. I am interested in data partly because I want to get better at communicating uncertainty to people who have to act on it.
recommendation_summary: Quiet, exact, and far more sophisticated in his thinking than his participation grade suggests.
financial_need_statement: First-generation. Family operates a small restaurant; income variable.

name: Abigail Shaw
extracurriculars: HOSA; nursing home volunteer; softball
essay_prompt: Describe a challenge you have faced and what you learned from it.
essay_text: I volunteered at a memory care facility for two years and for the first year I was doing it wrong. I kept correcting people. If a resident told me her husband was coming to pick her up and he had died in 2009, I would gently tell her. I thought honesty was the kind thing. A nurse pulled me aside and explained that I was making her grieve him again every single time. Now I ask what he was like. I still think about how confident I was that I was being good.
recommendation_summary: Unusually mature clinical instincts. Handles difficult situations with composure.
financial_need_statement: Household of four, one parent disabled and not working. High need.

essay_text: I have framed houses with my uncle every summer since eighth grade. Every single thing after that was slightly wrong and every crew made it slightly worse trying to fix the crew before them. We took it down. The owner was furious about the delay. I think about that inch and a half constantly. It is the cheapest thing in the world to fix on day one.
recommendation_summary: Practical, exacting, and carries real jobsite experience into the classroom.
financial_need_statement: Six-person household, first-generation, contributes significantly to family income.
